overall: The AG found a violation for an insufficiently specific April 16 notice that listed the wrong minutes date, found no violation on the executive session topic, and declined to review the mislabeled posting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Trust entered executive session at its April 16 meeting without listing an executive session topic on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Trust did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged where the notice for the April 16 meeting clearly listed an executive session topic to discuss an Open Meeting Law complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 16 notice listed the wrong date (February 12) for the minutes to be approved, when the Trust approved March 12 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: we nonetheless find that this error rendered the April 16 meeting notice insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Trust posted a mislabeled document online (the April 16 notice) in place of the April 16 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: an allegation that the Trust posted a mislabeled meeting notice rather than meeting minutes, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Trust’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
